title: Mini Shell (C)
description: A minimal Unix shell implementation with job control and piping
longDescription: Built a fully functional shell in C supporting command execution, pipelines (|), I/O redirection (<, >, >>), background jobs (&), and built-in commands (cd, exit, jobs, fg, bg). Implemented process management with fork/exec/wait, signal handling (SIGINT, SIGTSTP), and job control using process groups. Learned deep Unix process semantics and terminal control.

title: Linux Kernel Module
description: Character device driver with memory mapping and procfs interface
longDescription: Developed a loadable kernel module (LKM) creating a character device (/dev/mychar) with read/write/ioctl operations. Implemented memory-mapped I/O (mmap) for zero-copy user-kernel data transfer, procfs entry for runtime statistics, and proper synchronization with mutexes/spinlocks. Tested on x86_64 and ARM (Raspberry Pi). Gained hands-on experience with kernel memory management, interrupt context, and module lifecycle.

title: HTTP/1.1 Server from Scratch
description: Lightweight concurrent HTTP server in C with epoll
longDescription: Implemented a high-performance HTTP/1.1 server using Linux epoll for I/O multiplexing. Supports static file serving, directory listing, CGI execution, keep-alive connections, and chunked transfer encoding. Built custom thread pool for request handling, HTTP request/response parsing with zero-copy buffers, and graceful shutdown handling. Benchmarked against nginx for learning purposes.

title: System Process Monitor (Python)
longDescription: Terminal-based system monitor (like htop) built with Python and curses. Parses /proc filesystem for real-time CPU, memory, disk, and network stats per process. Features process tree visualization, filtering, sorting, and signal sending (SIGTERM, SIGKILL). Added customizable color themes and config file. Great exercise in Linux procfs internals and terminal UI programming.

title: x86 Bootloader (Assembly)
description: 16-bit real mode bootloader loading a 32-bit kernel
longDescription: Wrote a 512-byte bootloader in NASM assembly that initializes segment registers, enables A20 line, switches to protected mode, sets up GDT/IDT, and loads a simple 32-bit C kernel from disk. The kernel prints to screen using VGA text mode and handles keyboard interrupts. Built with QEMU for testing. Deep dive into x86 architecture, BIOS interrupts, and boot process.

title: Custom Memory Allocator
longDescription: Implemented a dynamic memory allocator in C using the buddy system algorithm. Supports malloc, free, calloc, realloc with proper alignment and coalescing. Added debugging features: memory leak detection, double-free detection, buffer overflow canaries, and allocation statistics. Integrated with LD_PRELOAD for drop-in replacement testing. Excellent exercise in pointer arithmetic, memory layout, and fragmentation handling.
